articles.body:
The money is wasted, yes.

If the company controls no regions, each of the commanders can only deploy in the port regions of their associated presidency.

A Commander can deploy their army to attack a region adjacent to their Presidency’s home region, yes? (Or are you talking about a different situation?) 
[/q]
Only if they already control the home region.

[q]Select a target. You may select your President's home region, any region associated with your Presidency, or any region that shares a border with a region associated with your Presidency.[/q]

"Region associated with your presidency" means a region you already successfully deployed in and control.[/q]
Ah, okay. And that understanding is based on the sentence in the paragraph on p. 23 regarding forming a Governorship from a successful Deploy in that region: [b]”That region is now associated with that President.”[/b] So, “associated” refers to [b]conquered[/b] regions (thus, a conquered Home Region is both Home Region and now “associated” with that Presidency). (I say “based on the sentence” since I haven’t yet spotted another area in the rules that explains this meaning of “associated.”)

articles.body:
That is the definition, yes. I suppose "associated with your presidency" is mechanically a region whose loot token is on the presidency, and this particular phrasing is used because armies aren't interchangeable (so "a conquered region" or similar would be insufficient definition).

I did miss the definition on a first read though, it does look like vague language on first glance, rather than something clearly defined.

No, that is incorrect. Home region is specifically called out as a separate definition from associated with presidency, as quoted above:

[q]You may select your President's home region, any region associated with your Presidency, or any region that shares a border with a region associated with your Presidency.[/q]

And also defined as being a region (even a home region) after a successful deploy, as quoted above:

[q]That region is now associated with that President.[/q]

articles.body:
OK, now I can see differences between scenarios.

In 1710 scenario at beginning there is no region associated with any presidency. Even all 3 home regions are not associated with their presidencies. All loot/control tokens are on the map in respective regions.
In this scenario Company should first take control over some home region/s. This will associate this region with it's presidency. Then this presidency can expand further to regions that shares a border with a region already associated with it.

In 1758 scenario only region of Bengal is Company controlled and associated with it's presidency. It's loot/control token is in Bengal presidency box and there is a red governor overlay in Bengal.

In 1813 scenario all home regions are Company controlled and associated with their presidencies. Their loot/control tokens are in respective presidency boxes. However there is no red governor overlay because Governor General is active in this scenario.
In this scenario a Presidency can right from the beginning of the game expand to regions that shares a border with a region already associated with it.
